question: Ashish has ₹1218 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Arun and Mahesh and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Arun and Mahesh got same amount after 11 and 12 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Ashish give to Mahesh?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When amounts are equal at Compound Interest, the ratio of the principals is directly related to the multiplying factors based on the time difference.

Ratio of Arun's share to Mahesh's share = (1 + 10/100)¹²−¹¹ : 1 = 11 : 10

Total ratio parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts

21 parts = ₹1218 ⇒ 1 part = ₹58

Mahesh's share = 10 parts = 10 × 58 = ₹580

**∴ The correct answer is ₹580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = ₹1218

Rate of interest (R) = 10% compounded annually

Time for Arun (T₁) = 11 years

Time for Mahesh (T₂) = 12 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ
